steps.title: Finding your way
steps.html:
Asking how to get somewhere — and explaining the way to someone else.

  • Ask for directions
  • Explain the way to a place
  • Use go past, turn left, on the corner

steps.title: Look at the two groups.
steps.prompt: What is the difference between the two groups?
options: The first group is about position, the second is about movement
The second group is about the past
steps.answer: The first group is about position, the second is about movement
steps.why: Some prepositions say where something is. Others say how you move.
steps.html:
Where it is: opposite the bank · between two streets · behind the building · on the corner

How you move: go along the street · go past the café · go through the park · turn into Albert Street

steps.title: Place and movement
steps.html:
PositionMovement
opposite the garagego along the street
between two streetsgo past the bank

in front of the windowturn into Albert Street
next to the supermarketgo up / down the hill
on the corner of the roadcross over the road

Directions in English are almost always imperatives: Go straight on. Turn left.

on the left tells you where it is; turn left tells you what to do.

Learners often say turn to left. The correct form is turn left.

Imperatives are the focus of Lesson 16.
